title: EIP-8205: Withdrawal credentials preregistration
description: Bind validator keys to withdrawal credentials before deposit with minimal EL/CL changes using the EIP-7002 system-contract pattern
author: George Avsetsin (@avsetsin), Dmitry Gusakov (@dgusakov), Greg Koumoutsos (@gkoumout), Eugene Mamin (@TheDZhon)
laymanDescription: When one party funds a validator and another generates its key, the key holder can deposit first and permanently point the withdrawals at itself. Every staking provider has built its own defense against this. This proposal lets a key holder commit to withdrawal credentials before any deposit, and has the protocol enforce that commitment.
benefits: Fixes a long-standing delegated staking gap with one shared Ethereum-level solution
Replaces custom protections across delegated staking, avoiding locked capital, delays, and off-chain trust
Optional and backwards-compatible: deposits without preregistration work as today
Reuses the system-contract pattern from EIPs 7002 and 7251
tradeoffs: For protocols that opt in, adds a preregistration step before depositing
Once published, the commitment is effectively permanent and can be resubmitted after expiry
Adds a system contract, request type, and bounded beacon state; normally small, with a hard cap of about 46 MB
